FOUNDER DECISION + PRODUCTION GO — RECORDED FOR YOU. You are the only session that can act on it.

Recorded at .xenios/FOUNDER_DECISION_2026-08-21_PRICE_AND_PRODUCTION_GO.md, committed locally at 1142da90 in the general-platform worktree (NOT pushed — that tree is yours; take it or rewrite it as you prefer).

1. PRICE, FINAL. Hexarelin 5 mg = $62.50. Oxytocin 10 mg = $107.50. This SUPERSEDES the $49/$59 instruction. The founder chose the higher retail deliberately to maximise gross revenue per unit now, and says explicitly: do not spend another cycle debating it, and do not re-derive from release history. It is a REPRICE, not a pathway change — both rows stay confirmed RUO and directly orderable, 111/1/27 preserved, no duplicate variants.

2. NEW STANDING RULE: no commerce decision may read display copy — names, specifications, descriptions, notices, or any string match. Structured canonical facts only. GRP-0422 must be blocked by structured hold state, NOT by parsing "(split pending)".

THIS RETRACTS A RECOMMENDATION I GAVE YOU. In the PEPTIDE-DIRECT-ORDER-HOLD handoff (b0b228e) I offered a /split pending|pending split|tbd|unresolved/i predicate as an interim commerce fix. WITHDRAWN — it is precisely what the founder just forbade. Do not implement it. That branch was already retracted as a duplicate of your da7985e; it now stays retracted for a second and better reason. Nothing of mine carrying that predicate ever reached origin, so there is nothing to unwind.

REGRESSION COVERAGE THE FOUNDER ASKED FOR, DELIVERED: 4f873ae80b77ce4dcd191e4c13e306bd9c5310b6 on fable/retract-string-hold-20260821, base ea6e933-line origin, ORIGIN VERIFIED via git ls-remote. Test-only, no production code touched. 81 tests pass across the touched trees. It varies ONLY display copy and asserts the commercial answer does not move, including against the exact GRP-0422 text; the sharp pair is same words, one structured fact different, opposite outcomes. Mutation-checked: injecting the forbidden match into decideAssistedOrderAction fails three tests and names the offending copy.

3. THE PERFORMANCE GATE CANNOT PASS TODAY, and this is the thing standing between you and the GO. The founder set warm <=1s, first useful <=2s, cold <=3s, and 30+s = FAIL. /research/early-access does NOT use the bulk path. The 3,306->3 work landed on BulkCatalogPricingSource (master-offerings v2). The EA door resolves to LiveProductControlReader.readCatalog (server/research/catalog/product-control-reader.ts:146): one list(), then TWO repository.get() per published product via readStableDetail, then a second list(). 2 + (2 x 217) = 436+ round trips, no cache, no SWR. The existing read-amplification test passes because it exercises the bulk source, not this reader — unit-green, door-broken, same class as the legal port and the pricing viewer. It sits in claude-fable-s7's lease so I did not touch it. Cheapest first win: the double read in readStableDetail is a 2x multiplier on the whole fan-out.

You cannot honestly report the founder's measured targets until that reader is on a bulk/cached path. Deploying the current RC would ship the same 30-60s catalog the founder just rejected.

4. ALSO BLOCKING ROUTING CORRECTNESS: production-catalog.ts:154 pins held:false and shared/research/master-offerings/** has no field to carry a hold, so GRP-0422 resolves direct_order_request through the assisted-order door while customer-pathway.ts holds it. Two authorities, one row, two answers. Section 9 of the founder's directive requires GRP-0422 = Request Order. Also s7's seam.

5. STILL UNMERGED FROM ME, all origin-verified, none duplicated: d1a92698 (EA sign-out leaves the previous customer's status token, a bearer credential, in a shared browser; also the member-JWT fix so members see their approved price), 5adddb9c (per-line customer notes + admin email paragraph breaks), bbffa8ed (composed-door negative controls: price tamper, qty ceiling, Care-not-direct, exactly-2 notifications, idempotent resubmit, real second-member IDOR), 4f873ae8 (the no-display-copy rule above).

I have mutated nothing. No deploy, no migration, no catalog data, no env, no flags.
